translations.answer: Due to differences in hand morphology between humans and robots, the same motion may result in completely different contacts. The C2Dex candidate solution involves recovering stable object-side contacts from monocular human videos and explicitly preserving them during retargeting; the post claims this covers 8 real-world tasks, but formal validation and code are still needed.
translations.applicability: Applicable to dexterous hands and contact-based operations during retargeting; not directly equivalent to full-body contact in bipedal systems.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is lacking.
translations.details.attempts.0: First, recover stable object-side contacts, then retarget with contact constraints.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Evaluate object-side contact preservation separately from pure pose matching.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The candidate method explicitly preserves object-side contact during retargeting.
translations.details.environments.0: Monocular human video; dexterous hand retargeting; 8 real-world tasks.
translations.details.limits.0: No failure rate, contact force error, or cross-hand type ablation; content is a paper abstract.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The post claims 24 video clips cover 8 real-world tasks.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Only matching kinematic poses may result in different contact geometries for human and robot hands.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before retargeting, limit force and check for penetration, joint limits, and object slippage.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Differences in robot morphology compared to human hands; same pose does not guarantee identical contact geometry.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Similar action trajectories but unstable or incorrect object-side contacts.
translations.media_summaries.0: Screenshot shows the problem statement and C2Dex mark, but no contact points, force curves, or retargeting failure comparison are displayed.
translations.source.title: Why Action Retargeting Can't Just Match Pose: Contact Consistency?
